claims.title: Megalith-building begins along the river
claims.summary: Communities in the Senegambian region began raising circles of cut laterite pillars and burial mounds along the Gambia River; excavated burials yield dates spanning roughly the third century BCE to the sixteenth century CE.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Gambia: From the megalithic stone circles and the Mandinka kingdoms of the river, through the Atlantic slave trade and a narrow British enclave inside French Senegal, to independence in 1965, the Jammeh years, and a democratic transition in 2017.", terralore.co/country/GMB/chronicle#ev-300bce-megalith-building-begins-along-the-river, claim TL:GMB:event:300bce:megalith-building-begins-along-the-river, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: A sacred landscape of more than a thousand monuments
claims.summary: Over fifteen centuries a prosperous, organised society created more than 1,000 stone circles and tumuli across a band some 100 km wide along 350 km of the river; burials near Wassu date to roughly AD 900–1300.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Gambia: From the megalithic stone circles and the Mandinka kingdoms of the river, through the Atlantic slave trade and a narrow British enclave inside French Senegal, to independence in 1965, the Jammeh years, and a democratic transition in 2017.", terralore.co/country/GMB/chronicle#ev-900-a-sacred-landscape-of-more-than-a-thousand, claim TL:GMB:event:900:a-sacred-landscape-of-more-than-a-thousand, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Settlement of the Mandinka, Wolof, Fula and Serer
claims.summary: The ancestors of the region's principal peoples — Mandinka, Wolof, Fula and Serer — settled the river valley and savanna through migration and the spread of farming, herding and trade, predating the river kingdoms.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Gambia: From the megalithic stone circles and the Mandinka kingdoms of the river, through the Atlantic slave trade and a narrow British enclave inside French Senegal, to independence in 1965, the Jammeh years, and a democratic transition in 2017.", terralore.co/country/GMB/chronicle#ev-1000-settlement-of-the-mandinka-wolof-fula-and-serer, claim TL:GMB:event:1000:settlement-of-the-mandinka-wolof-fula-and-serer, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mali's reach extends to the Gambia
claims.summary: The Mali Empire expanded into the Gambia River valley in the thirteenth century, bringing the region within the Mande world and spreading Islam, trade and administration as Mandinka traders moved west.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Gambia: From the megalithic stone circles and the Mandinka kingdoms of the river, through the Atlantic slave trade and a narrow British enclave inside French Senegal, to independence in 1965, the Jammeh years, and a democratic transition in 2017.", terralore.co/country/GMB/chronicle#ev-1235-mali-s-reach-extends-to-the-gambia, claim TL:GMB:event:1235:mali-s-reach-extends-to-the-gambia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mandinka kingdoms of the river
claims.summary: Mandinka warriors and traders founded small states along both banks of the Gambia, including Niumi (Barra), Niani and Wuli, which controlled river trade and important inland routes.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Gambia: From the megalithic stone circles and the Mandinka kingdoms of the river, through the Atlantic slave trade and a narrow British enclave inside French Senegal, to independence in 1965, the Jammeh years, and a democratic transition in 2017.", terralore.co/country/GMB/chronicle#ev-1300-mandinka-kingdoms-of-the-river, claim TL:GMB:event:1300:mandinka-kingdoms-of-the-river, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Niumi commands the river mouth
claims.summary: The Mandinka kingdom of Niumi, controlled in rotation by clans such as the Jamme, Maane and Sonko, grew prosperous by taxing merchant traffic at the mouth of the Gambia River and would later levy tolls on European vessels.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Gambia: From the megalithic stone circles and the Mandinka kingdoms of the river, through the Atlantic slave trade and a narrow British enclave inside French Senegal, to independence in 1965, the Jammeh years, and a democratic transition in 2017.", terralore.co/country/GMB/chronicle#ev-1400-niumi-commands-the-river-mouth, claim TL:GMB:event:1400:niumi-commands-the-river-mouth, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Portuguese ships enter the Gambia
claims.summary: Expeditions under Cadamosto and Usodimare, sailing for Portugal's Prince Henry the Navigator, reached the Gambia River and opened European trade, establishing the first contacts and small settlements along its banks.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Gambia: From the megalithic stone circles and the Mandinka kingdoms of the river, through the Atlantic slave trade and a narrow British enclave inside French Senegal, to independence in 1965, the Jammeh years, and a democratic transition in 2017.", terralore.co/country/GMB/chronicle#ev-1455-portuguese-ships-enter-the-gambia, claim TL:GMB:event:1455:portuguese-ships-enter-the-gambia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: England takes James Island
claims.summary: English forces seized the midstream island, renaming it James Island and building Fort James; chartered companies ran the post, and its trade shifted from gold and ivory toward enslaved Africans.

sources.label: Kunta Kinteh Island and Related Sites

claims.title: The Atlantic slave trade on the river
claims.summary: James Island, with the villages of Juffure and Albreda, became a major slaving station; captives from the interior were held there before being shipped across the Atlantic, while England and France fought repeatedly for control of the river.

sources.label: Kunta Kinteh Island and Related Sites

claims.title: Britain abolishes its slave trade
claims.summary: Britain outlawed its transatlantic slave trade and later built defences such as Fort Bullen at the river mouth to help suppress slaving — among the few regional structures built against the trade rather than for it.

sources.label: Kunta Kinteh Island and Related Sites

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Gambia: From the megalithic stone circles and the Mandinka kingdoms of the river, through the Atlantic slave trade and a narrow British enclave inside French Senegal, to independence in 1965, the Jammeh years, and a democratic transition in 2017.", terralore.co/country/GMB/chronicle#ev-1807-britain-abolishes-its-slave-trade, claim TL:GMB:event:1807:britain-abolishes-its-slave-trade, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Kunta Kinteh Island recognised
claims.summary: James Island and Related Sites were inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2003 as a memorial to the slave trade; the island was renamed Kunta Kinteh Island in 2011, recalling the figure in Alex Haley's Roots associated with nearby Juffure.

sources.label: Kunta Kinteh Island and Related Sites

claims.title: Bathurst founded on St Mary's Island
claims.summary: Captain Alexander Grant established the settlement of Bathurst (now Banjul) near the mouth of the Gambia, creating Britain's base for suppressing the slave trade and trading in groundnuts.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Gambia: From the megalithic stone circles and the Mandinka kingdoms of the river, through the Atlantic slave trade and a narrow British enclave inside French Senegal, to independence in 1965, the Jammeh years, and a democratic transition in 2017.", terralore.co/country/GMB/chronicle#ev-1816-bathurst-founded-on-st-mary-s-island, claim TL:GMB:event:1816:bathurst-founded-on-st-mary-s-island, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Anglo-French agreements draw the enclave
claims.summary: Boundary agreements between Britain and France fixed The Gambia's frontiers as a narrow band following the river, leaving the territory almost entirely surrounded by French Senegal.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Gambia: From the megalithic stone circles and the Mandinka kingdoms of the river, through the Atlantic slave trade and a narrow British enclave inside French Senegal, to independence in 1965, the Jammeh years, and a democratic transition in 2017.", terralore.co/country/GMB/chronicle#ev-1889-anglo-french-agreements-draw-the-enclave, claim TL:GMB:event:1889:anglo-french-agreements-draw-the-enclave, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Colony and Protectorate established
claims.summary: Britain organised its possession into the Colony of the Gambia, centred on Bathurst, and a larger inland Protectorate governed indirectly through local chiefs, completing the colonial framework.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Gambia: From the megalithic stone circles and the Mandinka kingdoms of the river, through the Atlantic slave trade and a narrow British enclave inside French Senegal, to independence in 1965, the Jammeh years, and a democratic transition in 2017.", terralore.co/country/GMB/chronicle#ev-1902-colony-and-protectorate-established, claim TL:GMB:event:1902:colony-and-protectorate-established, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Jawara leads toward self-rule
claims.summary: After a new 1960 constitution created a House of Representatives, Dawda Jawara of the People's Progressive Party became premier in 1962, leading the colony through internal self-government toward independence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Gambia: From the megalithic stone circles and the Mandinka kingdoms of the river, through the Atlantic slave trade and a narrow British enclave inside French Senegal, to independence in 1965, the Jammeh years, and a democratic transition in 2017.", terralore.co/country/GMB/chronicle#ev-1962-jawara-leads-toward-self-rule, claim TL:GMB:event:1962:jawara-leads-toward-self-rule, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence from the United Kingdom
claims.summary: The Gambia became independent within the Commonwealth as a constitutional monarchy, with Dawda Jawara as prime minister; the United States acknowledged independence the same day at ceremonies in Bathurst.

sources.label: A Guide to the History of Recognition: The Gambia
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: The Gambia becomes a republic
claims.summary: After a second referendum, The Gambia adopted a republican constitution and Dawda Jawara became its first president, severing the last formal ties of British sovereignty.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Gambia: From the megalithic stone circles and the Mandinka kingdoms of the river, through the Atlantic slave trade and a narrow British enclave inside French Senegal, to independence in 1965, the Jammeh years, and a democratic transition in 2017.", terralore.co/country/GMB/chronicle#ev-1970-the-gambia-becomes-a-republic, claim TL:GMB:event:1970:the-gambia-becomes-a-republic, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Coup attempt and Senegalese intervention
claims.summary: A violent attempt to seize power led by Kukoi Samba Sanyang briefly took Bathurst while Jawara was abroad; Senegalese troops intervened under a defence pact to crush the revolt and restore him.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Gambia: From the megalithic stone circles and the Mandinka kingdoms of the river, through the Atlantic slave trade and a narrow British enclave inside French Senegal, to independence in 1965, the Jammeh years, and a democratic transition in 2017.", terralore.co/country/GMB/chronicle#ev-1981-coup-attempt-and-senegalese-intervention, claim TL:GMB:event:1981:coup-attempt-and-senegalese-intervention, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Senegambia Confederation formed
claims.summary: The Gambia and Senegal established the Senegambia Confederation to integrate their militaries, security and economies while retaining sovereignty, with Senegal's Abdou Diouf as president and Jawara as vice-president.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Gambia: From the megalithic stone circles and the Mandinka kingdoms of the river, through the Atlantic slave trade and a narrow British enclave inside French Senegal, to independence in 1965, the Jammeh years, and a democratic transition in 2017.", terralore.co/country/GMB/chronicle#ev-1982-the-senegambia-confederation-formed, claim TL:GMB:event:1982:the-senegambia-confederation-formed, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The confederation dissolves
claims.summary: Lacking popular support and strained by disputes over economic and customs integration, the Senegambia Confederation was formally dissolved after Senegal withdrew its troops, and the two states resumed separate paths.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Gambia: From the megalithic stone circles and the Mandinka kingdoms of the river, through the Atlantic slave trade and a narrow British enclave inside French Senegal, to independence in 1965, the Jammeh years, and a democratic transition in 2017.", terralore.co/country/GMB/chronicle#ev-1989-the-confederation-dissolves, claim TL:GMB:event:1989:the-confederation-dissolves, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Jammeh's coup ends the Jawara era
claims.summary: Lieutenant Yahya Jammeh and fellow officers overthrew President Dawda Jawara in a bloodless coup, installing a military council and ending the only government independent Gambia had known.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Gambia: From the megalithic stone circles and the Mandinka kingdoms of the river, through the Atlantic slave trade and a narrow British enclave inside French Senegal, to independence in 1965, the Jammeh years, and a democratic transition in 2017.", terralore.co/country/GMB/chronicle#ev-1994-jammeh-s-coup-ends-the-jawara-era, claim TL:GMB:event:1994:jammeh-s-coup-ends-the-jawara-era, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Jammeh elected president
claims.summary: After a transition to civilian rule under a new constitution, Jammeh was declared winner of the 1996 presidential election and sworn in, beginning a tenure he would extend through further votes in 2001, 2006 and 2011.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Gambia: From the megalithic stone circles and the Mandinka kingdoms of the river, through the Atlantic slave trade and a narrow British enclave inside French Senegal, to independence in 1965, the Jammeh years, and a democratic transition in 2017.", terralore.co/country/GMB/chronicle#ev-1996-jammeh-elected-president, claim TL:GMB:event:1996:jammeh-elected-president, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Repression and abuses under Jammeh
claims.summary: Jammeh's rule was marked by suppression of the press, detentions, torture, enforced disappearances and a 2009 witch-hunting campaign; a later Truth, Reconciliation and Reparations Commission documented widespread abuses.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Gambia: From the megalithic stone circles and the Mandinka kingdoms of the river, through the Atlantic slave trade and a narrow British enclave inside French Senegal, to independence in 1965, the Jammeh years, and a democratic transition in 2017.", terralore.co/country/GMB/chronicle#ev-2009-repression-and-abuses-under-jammeh, claim TL:GMB:event:2009:repression-and-abuses-under-jammeh, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Barrow defeats Jammeh
claims.summary: Adama Barrow, backed by an opposition coalition, won the presidential election; Jammeh initially conceded but a week later rejected the result, precipitating a constitutional crisis.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Gambia: From the megalithic stone circles and the Mandinka kingdoms of the river, through the Atlantic slave trade and a narrow British enclave inside French Senegal, to independence in 1965, the Jammeh years, and a democratic transition in 2017.", terralore.co/country/GMB/chronicle#ev-2016-barrow-defeats-jammeh, claim TL:GMB:event:2016:barrow-defeats-jammeh, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: ECOWAS intervention and transfer of power
claims.summary: Barrow was sworn in at the Gambian embassy in Dakar on 19 January 2017; with ECOWAS troops deployed under UN authorisation, Jammeh agreed to leave and went into exile in Equatorial Guinea on 21 January, completing a peaceful handover.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Gambia: From the megalithic stone circles and the Mandinka kingdoms of the river, through the Atlantic slave trade and a narrow British enclave inside French Senegal, to independence in 1965, the Jammeh years, and a democratic transition in 2017.", terralore.co/country/GMB/chronicle#ev-2017-ecowas-intervention-and-transfer-of-power, claim TL:GMB:event:2017:ecowas-intervention-and-transfer-of-power, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
